passing: A strategy passes only if it beats holding the same coin at the same average exposure on Sharpe, after costs, and its deflated Sharpe clears the bar. Lower drawdown alone is not an edge: holding less of the coin gives it for free. Drawdown is a limit, not a goal.

scorecard.name: Edge
scorecard.rule: Sharpe beats holding the same coin at the same average exposure, after costs.
scorecard.why: Being out of the market some of the time is free; only a better return per unit of risk is skill.

scorecard.name: Luck
scorecard.rule: Deflated Sharpe at least 95%, counting every trial.
scorecard.why: The best of many worthless strategies looks good by chance; this corrects for how many were tried.

scorecard.name: Out of sample
scorecard.rule: Walk-forward: most test windows still beat exposure-matched holding.
scorecard.why: Settings chosen on the past must keep working on months they never saw.

scorecard.name: Start dates
scorecard.rule: Beats exposure-matched holding in at least 50% of 2-year start windows.
scorecard.why: A result that depends on starting in one lucky year isn't one you could have had.

scorecard.name: Costs
scorecard.rule: Break-even cost at least 2x the actual cost.
scorecard.why: Real fills will be worse than modelled; the edge needs room to absorb that.

scorecard.name: Enough trades
scorecard.why: Fewer trades than this can't tell skill from a few good bets.

scorecard.name: Drawdown limit
scorecard.why: A strategy you would abandon halfway down earns nothing.

scorecard.name: Robustness
scorecard.rule: Neighbouring settings also pass the edge test.
scorecard.why: A plateau of good settings is a pattern; a single peak is noise that was fitted.

scorecard.name: Random entry
scorecard.rule: Bracket strategies: net expectancy per trade beats at least 95% of random-entry paths with the same stops, targets and sizing.
scorecard.why: A 4R win against a 1R loss looks good whatever picks the entry; only beating random entries shows the entries matter. Added 2026-11-15 (Luke's YouTube spec).

risk_managed: A strategy that hasn't passed but is kept because it smooths the ride. It is labelled 'not a proven edge' and never counts as a pass. Trend-vol-target on BTC goes to paper trading on this basis: it beat holding BTC at the same exposure, and passed the holdout, but didn't clear the luck bar.
entry_bar: Who pays you and why: an economic reason, not a chart pattern.
Outside evidence: a published or out-of-sample result from somewhere else.
If it revives a rejected family: the earlier note, the failure mode it addresses and its one change, named before any run (one revival per failure mode).
How many runs it will use, declared before any run.
account: Research at the real account size (about A$500, 330 USDT). Binance refuses orders under 5 USDT, so a strategy holds at most 3 coins at once.

lessons.title: Trend rules limit losses; two beat holding, neither by enough.
lessons.text: Trend following, a trend basket and weekly momentum all cut drawdowns, often by half. Trend following on BTC and weekly momentum on ETH also beat the same coin held at the same exposure, but by margins that 175 trials could produce by chance, and trend following won only 2 of 7 six-month windows out of sample.

lessons.title: The trend votes carry it, not the sizing.
lessons.text: The same volatility sizing without the trend votes (vol-hold) scored a Sharpe of 0.93 on BTC, below holding.

lessons.title: Reversal, pullback and chart-pattern rules failed.
lessons.text: Structure pullbacks, pivot reversals, buying big down days, a Fear & Greed contrarian rule and four chart patterns: none was convincingly better than zero after costs, and each was worse than its simpler control (a plain breakout, a plain pullback).

lessons.title: Results on one coin and period rarely repeat.
lessons.text: Weekly momentum passed every test on ETH 2020-25, then failed on BTC, on ETH 2017-19 and on SOL. Channel breakout was robust to its settings but failed walk-forward on both coins.

lessons.title: Baskets of large coins are worse than BTC alone.
lessons.text: And at 330 USDT a basket's slots are too small to trade: 13.6% of the trend basket's orders were below Binance's minimum.

lessons.title: No lead from BTC at a weekly lag.
lessons.text: BTC's week was no better a signal for ETH or SOL than their own.

lessons.title: Stops made the survivors worse.
lessons.text: A 2 ATR trailing crash brake on weekly momentum (ETH) and trend-vol-target (BTC) lowered both Sharpes (1.23 to 1.21, 1.21 to 0.91) and barely moved drawdowns. Most trips sold a dip that recovered; crypto's normal swings are wider than a stop that tight, and the strategies' own exits already do the job.

lessons.title: Trend-vol-target already avoids volatile markets.
lessons.text: A filter that stepped out whenever the regime model (an HMM) said the market was in its volatile state lowered the Sharpe (0.64 vs 0.69): on those days the strategy already held 13% on average, against 54% on others, because its trend votes and volatility sizing do the same job.

lessons.title: In volatile spells, MACD's direction continued (a study, not yet a strategy).
lessons.text: On days the regime model called volatile, the week after a positive MACD histogram returned +1.63% on average and the week after a negative one -2.00% (BTC and ETH, 2021-25, 75 non-overlapping weeks, P = 98%); on other days the relationship slightly reversed. The coins move together, so the sample is smaller than it looks. As a long-only strategy it failed (BTC Sharpe -0.13, ETH 0.42 against 0.46 for holding at its exposure, 19-26 trades): most of the spread was the down weeks, which a long-only account can only sit out, and sitting out is what holding less does for free. A short side would change that.

lessons.title: Attention and extreme fear don't pick better weeks.
lessons.text: Weeks after rising Wikipedia attention returned +0.65% against +0.74% for the rest (854 weeks, BTC and ETH 2017-25); weeks after Extreme Fear returned +0.27% against +0.59% (806 weeks). Liu and Tsyvinski's attention effect didn't appear with this stand-in for Google searches, and fear mostly followed falls that continued: in crypto, moves tend to carry on, and buying fear or dips keeps losing.

lessons.title: After a Binance delisting announcement, coins keep falling until removal (a study).
lessons.text: Across 21 announcements (80 coins, 2022-10 to 2025-09), a coin bought at the open the day after the announcement and sold at the removal day's open lost 39.8% on average (41.9% more than BTC over the same days); 18 of 21 announcements fell, P(mean < 0) 100%. That comes after a 31% fall on the announcement day itself and a 16% lag behind BTC over the 30 days before. There was no rebound to buy: the pre-registered verdict is EXIT RULE (sell at once), not REBOUND. For a long-only account this is a safety rule for any strategy holding small coins, not an edge; only a short could earn the fall (P5). 30 of 110 announced coins couldn't be measured, most because their USDT pair had already gone. A hypothetical perp short (pre-registered, 2x with liquidations) was INSUFFICIENT: of the 80 coins, 50 had no USDT-M perp and 16 had a perp that stopped trading before the spot removal, so only 12 coins in 6 announcements could be shorted to the end (10 announcements needed). Those 12 averaged -7.8% net at 2x (P > 0: 29%): shorts paid 1.2% in funding, and 3 of 12 were liquidated, including HIFI's +1,357% squeeze during its window in 2025-09. The fall is real, but on Binance it was mostly not shortable, and where it was, a crowded short got squeezed.

lessons.title: Trend-vol-target hasn't been shown outside crypto.
lessons.text: Run unchanged on gold, EUR and GBP (2026-11-16), it lost to holding gold at the same exposure and lost money on both currencies. Its edge is shown only on BTC, ETH and SOL, which trended hard in 2020-25; time-series momentum's long record in commodities and currencies didn't show up here in five years of daily bars.

lessons.title: Searching freely, then confirming on unsearched coins, found one rule that held up (the exploration experiment, 2026-11-16).
lessons.text: About 230 daily rules were searched on 181 exploration coins (not trials, not evidence); two graduated, and each was run once on the 180 confirmation coins nobody had looked at. Holding an altcoin only while BTC is above its 50-day average and the coin is up over 30 days, sized to 50% volatility, beat holding on 149 of 180 coins (83%) and won 427 of 771 walk-forward windows (55%): PASS. Buying a 30% weekly crash for 3 days beat holding on 62% of coins but won only 36% of windows: FAIL. Caveats: most altcoins lost about 90% in 2020-25, so beating them on Sharpe is a low bar, and 55% of windows is a narrow margin; the rule leans on BTC's trend, as trend-vol-target does. A pass is not a pursue: it still needs its own scorecard, a rule for which coins to hold, and a holdout test. Run unchanged on ETH and SOL (2026-11-16; heavily searched coins, so not a confirmation), it beat holding at the same exposure and trend-vol-target on both (Sharpe 1.33 and 1.72) with drawdowns near -33%, and passed walk-forward and robustness; it fails only luck against the main bar, and both coins' holdout years are already spent. Pursued to paper trading (Claude's call, delegated by Luke).

lessons.title: Neither funding nor taker flow picks next week's winners among liquid coins (2026-11-16, after an outside review proposed market-structure signals).
lessons.text: On the exploration half plus BTC, ETH and SOL, 234 Sunday closes (2020-09 to 2025-10, a median of 19 liquid coins a week), with past week and size as controls: buyer-led taker flow had a slope of +0.17% a week per SD (P 86%, 90% needed) and its top fifth beat the average coin by 0.52% a week, but as money that top fifth lost 38% after costs (drawdown -92%) because the average liquid altcoin lost 57%; most of its edge was the past week's rise. Low funding (the uncrowded side) did worse, not better: slope -0.26% a week per SD (P(> 0) 9%), and its top fifth lost 87% after costs; the crowded side lost 53%. Long-only, both are only coin pickers, and only inside a rule that already decides when to hold altcoins at all; the BTC regime rule is the candidate.

lessons.title: A BTC-regime momentum rotation passed a holdout year on coins it had never seen (2026-11-16).
lessons.text: Exploration round 2 searched 1,760 rotation settings on BTC, ETH, SOL and large exploration-half coins (not evidence): the BTC 50-day filter did most of the work, and under it 90-day momentum picks beat random picks. Two graduates, each weekly while BTC closes 3% above its 50-day average and volatility-sized, were run once on the unspent holdout year of BTC plus the largest confirmation-half coins, chosen by volume alone. Holding the top 3 of 8 finished flat while BTC fell 29% (BTC at its 18% exposure: -4.7%), worst drawdown -11%: PASS. Holding only the top 1 of 4 lost 22.6% (BTC at its exposure -5.7%): FAIL; one coin was too concentrated. One falling year and about 50 weekly decisions: support for forward paper trading, not proof. G1's full scorecard on its own coins (2018-25) fails only luck and walk-forward (5 of 11 windows, its out-of-sample Sharpe equal to in-sample): trend-vol-target's standard, with a pass on unseen coins added. **Survivorship (disclosed 2026-11-16, after an outside review):** G1's 8 coins are today's large coins, picked in 2026. Its 2018-25 backtest never holds a coin before it lists, but it only contains coins that went on to succeed (SOL and DOT didn't exist in 2018; large coins of 2018 that faded aren't in it), so those numbers flatter it. The holdout year is clean of this: that basket was fixed from volume before 2025-11.

lessons.title: The pursued strategies are mostly one bet: long crypto while it trends up (2026-11-16, `kestrel overlap`).
lessons.text: Daily returns of the six pursued runs (trend-vol-target on BTC, ETH, SOL; btc-regime-trend on ETH, SOL; G1), 2020-08-13 to 2025-10-31 (1,907 days), read from saved runs (no trials). Correlation follows the coin, not the strategy: trend-vol-target and btc-regime-trend correlate 0.82 on ETH and 0.83 on SOL, 0.35-0.69 across coins; G1 0.42-0.58 with each. BTC explains 64% of trend-vol-target BTC's daily variance, 39% on ETH, 8-23% for the rest (betas 0.18-0.45). By BTC's month, all six earn only in rising months (+0.30 to +0.40% a day) and lose in falling ones (-0.06 to -0.22% a day), except G1 (+0.01%); flat months are flat. On BTC's 206 worst days (down over 3%) their link to BTC weakens (mostly in cash), but G1 and btc-regime-trend ETH move together more (0.73). An equal mix has a Sharpe of 1.79 against 1.73 for the best alone; it rises without trend-vol-target ETH (1.87) or BTC (1.81). In-sample Sharpes of selected strategies, so optimistic; this decides nothing, but a second edge has to come from somewhere other than trend.

lessons.title: Shorting the trend doesn't pay; collecting funding does (hypothetical, 2026-11-16, `kestrel short-study`).
lessons.text: Five frozen notes, each run once on 2020-01 to 2025-10 (funding history starts 2020), costed as a 2:1 CFD (2x the spread band, 5% a year financing) with a Binance perp reported. Adding a short side to every pursued trend rule made it worse: btc-regime-trend's mirror short on ETH and SOL (Sharpe 1.30 and 1.35 against 1.47 and 1.64 long-only; short legs +13% and +6%, P 72% and 68%), G1 shorting its 3 weakest coins (1.13 against 1.66; short leg -49%) and symmetric trend-vol-target (0.82-0.97 against 1.23-1.45; short legs -35% to -46%). Each beat its long-only rule only in 2022, the one long bear year, and lost to it in the others: crypto's rebounds take back what the shorts make. Long/short momentum among liquid coins (top 3 against bottom 3, weekly, near market-neutral: beta -0.05) made +39% in six years (Sharpe 0.44, P 84%, 95% needed), all from the long leg (+119%; shorts -50%): FAIL. **Cash-and-carry passed every test**: holding BTC, ETH and SOL against their perps while the last week's funding was positive earned +6.6% a year on equity, positive in 5 of 6 years (2022 -5.9%, when funding turned negative), drawdown -6.6%, 53 trades, 14 margin calls. It is a collection of leveraged longs' funding, not a price bet. Caveats: the spot-perp basis isn't modelled (perp prices aren't stored), so the drawdown is a floor; Schmeling, Schrimpf and Todorov (BIS 2023) find high carry predicts crashes; at 330 USDT each hedge is about 73 USDT, which may be under a perp's minimum order (unchecked); and it needs a real perp, wholesale-only in Australia today. 8 trials (846 in all; luck bar 2.30).

lessons.title: A coin's first perp listing marks a local top (a study, 2026-11-18, `kestrel event-study perp-listing`).
lessons.text: 102 coins of the exploration half (plus BTC, ETH, SOL) whose Binance USDT-M perp first settled funding from 2020-01 on, with 60+ days of spot before it. In the 30 days before the listing they rose +100% on average against the other coins; in the 30 days after (from day 1's open) they lagged the other coins by -15.2% on average (P(< 0) 100%; 75% of events below zero), every year from -2.7% (2022, 6 events) to -23.4% (2021), and worse than all 200 placebo draws of the same coins on random days (placebo median -1.3%): EXIT RULE by the note. Robustness, deciding nothing: against the median other coin -5.5% (median event -9.8%, 68% below zero), against BTC -7.9% (median -17.5%); the coin's own return averaged +1.5% (median -8.3%), so the rule is about relative weakness, not a guaranteed fall. For an altcoin portfolio: don't buy a coin, or hold it, through its first month of perps. Who pays, as the note argued: the perp lets pessimists in after a run (Hale et al. 2018 on Bitcoin's CME launch). The first run was void (findings, Mistakes). As a trade it fails (note shorting-new-perp-listings-hedged-with-btc, hypothetical, 2026-11-18): shorting each new perp for 30 days against an equal BTC long, 3 at a time, made +11% in six years (Sharpe 0.25), mean trade +2.3% on its slot (P 80%, 95% needed), positive in 3 of 6 years, drawdown -56%. Three things ate the edge: 15 squeezes closed shorts out at +50% in a day, new perps' negative funding cost 18% of equity (crowded shorts pay), and 29 of 102 events found the book full. Unhedged, the short lost 68%. DROP: the effect is real as a reason not to hold a coin, not as a short.

lessons.title: Large token unlocks don't show a drift we can use (a study, 2026-11-21, `kestrel event-study token-unlocks`).
lessons.text: DefiLlama's public unlock schedules (375 protocols), mapped to Binance coins by a strict ticker rule (any ticker shared by two CoinGecko ids dropped), left 122 unlocks of at least 2% of the unlocked supply on 12 exploration-half coins, 2020-25. In the 30 days before the unlock they did +0.4% against the other coins (P(< 0) 47%; 63% of events below zero): KILL. The same coins on random days did worse (placebo median -4.5%): these coins lag in general, and the unlocks add nothing. Deciding nothing: -3.1% in the last two weeks; insider unlocks (team, investors) -7.1% but only 7 events; unlocks large for the coin's daily volume -2.1% against +2.6% for small ones. The published "90% of unlocks fall" (Keyrock) is mostly about coins that fall anyway. Caveats: 12 coins (the ticker rule was strict); schedules as documented today.

lessons.title: An altcoin portfolio on the BTC regime, with the exit rules, is worse than holding a little BTC (2026-11-21, note altcoin-portfolio-on-the-btc-regime-with-exit).
lessons.text: G1's weekly rule on a point-in-time universe (exploration-half coins with 20M USDT a day and a year of history, a median of 14 a week), top 3 by 90-day return while BTC is 3% above its 50-day average, selling on a delisting announcement or a new perp. 2019-01 to 2025-10 (2019 in cash by construction: a year of history first): +101%, Sharpe 0.53, drawdown -33%, 17% exposure, 433 trades, costs 7.8x covered. The note's edge test, against the large-basket control on the same coins (+39%, Sharpe 0.44, drawdown -85%), passes narrowly, and all six neighbours (top 2/4, 60/120 days, 2%/4%) beat it too (0.46-0.70). But BTC held at the same 17% exposure made +113% (Sharpe 1.10); walk-forward beat holding in 3 of 9 windows; 2-year starts 32%; luck 0%. Not every test but luck, so no holdout test by the note. Picking altcoins under the BTC regime adds turnover and alt risk for less than a small BTC position gives. 16 trials (863 in all; luck bar 2.28).

lessons.title: Tori Trades' trendline method doesn't beat holding at the same exposure (2026-11-21, note tori-trades-trendline-method-long-only; Luke's request, a rejected family, disclosed).
lessons.text: Long only, mechanical: buy a close above a falling line through swing highs touched 3+ times; stop at the low the break started from; no target, exit on a close below the new rising line. BTC, ETH, SOL 4h, 2020-25: +26%, +45%, +65% (Sharpe 0.41, 0.57, 0.82), drawdowns -18% to -25%, 212-247 trades, +0.17R to +0.40R a trade after costs; but in the market only 6-10% of the time, and the coin held at that same exposure did better on Sharpe every time (1.07, 1.12, 1.24). Fails test 1 on all three: drop by the note. Her exit (no target, a trailing line) did better than our earlier trendline tests' fixed 3R targets (those lost money), but not enough to beat simply holding a little of the coin. Grids skipped for a strategy failing test 1 (Luke's standing rule). 3 trials.

lessons.title: Three non-trend signals don't pick better weeks once past weeks are controlled for (2026-11-22, `kestrel signal-study`; notes does-us-buying-on-coinbase-lead-prices, does-a-high-variance-premium-lead-prices, does-dollar-liquidity-lead-crypto).
lessons.text: Chosen to be independent of the trend bet (findings 16), each pre-registered with a control: the spread must be positive both after a rising and after a falling past week. BTC and ETH pooled, Sunday closes, one run each: - US buying on Coinbase (its 7-day premium over Binance, USDT-adjusted, above its 180-day median), 2021-11 to 2025-10: spread +0.67% a week, P 79% (90% needed); +1.42% after a falling week, -0.35% after a rising one: KILL. A rebound effect, not a demand signal. - A high variance premium (Deribit DVOL less 30-day realised volatility, the same rule), 2021-09 to 2025-10: +0.73%, P 81%; +1.45% after falls, -0.20% after rises: KILL, the dip-buying family in disguise, as the note warned. - Dollar net liquidity growing over 4 weeks (Fed assets less the Treasury account and reverse repo), 2018-01 to 2025-10: -0.71%, P 17%, negative after rises and falls alike: KILL; weeks after liquidity grew were worse. Matches the New York Fed's finding that Bitcoin doesn't respond to rate surprises. Deciding nothing, by its note: the Coinbase premium from 2018 with USDT taken as a dollar passed (spread +1.32%, P 96%, positive after rises and falls). It can't count: it was labelled beside the result before the run, and its extra years (2018 to early 2021) are when USDT itself swung, so there the "premium" is partly fear of USDT. Pursuing it would need a new note, disclosed as chosen after a look, judged forward only.

lessons.title: The regime preset is already the right model, and faster regimes warn early but mostly falsely (2026-11-22, research/regimes/; descriptions, not trials).
lessons.text: Variants of the HMM were compared by out-of-sample likelihood, walking forward month by month on BTC and ETH before the holdout, each scored on the same days and the same shared inputs. Scored on return and volatility together, 5 states beat the preset's 3 by 0.26-0.37 nats a day; volume, distance from the 1-year high and (for ETH) BTC's inputs all made it worse; a shorter window helped BTC and hurt ETH. Scored on returns alone, no variant beat the preset by more than 0.002 nats a day and on ETH all were worse: the extra states only track slow-moving 20-day volatility more finely. The preset (3 states, 4 years) stays. Faster models (the same shape on 4h and 1h bars, 20-bar volatility, a 1-year window), 2021-01 to 2025-10: the daily model had 11-12 volatile spells of about three weeks. A 4h model was volatile 27% of the time in about 115 spells of 3.5 days; it was volatile in the week before 82-100% of daily onsets (about 50% would be chance at that rate), starting a median 40-44 hours earlier, but 72-80% of its spells were never confirmed by a daily close within a week. The 1h model flickers (about 430 spells, 20 hours each; calling 100% of onsets is near chance, about 85%). A real early warning at 4h, three times in four a false one; trading on it would need its own note.

lessons.title: Stepping out on the 4h model's warnings made trend-vol-target worse on every coin (2026-11-23, note `trend-vol-target-out-in-the-4h-volatile-regime`; 6 trials, 872 in all, luck bar 2.27).
lessons.text: The daily filter (finding 8) failed because it came too late; the 4h model warns ~40 hours earlier, so it was given one try, pre-registered to pass on 2 of 3 coins. Filter on vs off, same days: BTC Sharpe 0.41 vs 0.64 (2020-12 to 2025-10), ETH 0.63 vs 0.72, SOL 0.12 vs 0.78 (2021-08 to 2025-10); returns +43% vs +104%, +100% vs +152%, -2% vs +138%. Drawdown was barely shallower on BTC (-46.8% vs -48.0%) and SOL (-35.6% vs -36.4%), deeper on ETH (-42% vs -38%). It traded no more often but turned over 1.3-1.7x as much (it sells whole positions); costs rose 26% on BTC and 43% on ETH, and on SOL the break-even cost fell below the actual one (18 vs 22 bps). The false alarms sell good days: being out when the 4h model is volatile misses rebounds as well as falls. Regime timing does not help this rule at either speed; its own trend votes and volatility sizing already do the job.

lessons.title: Forex trend lost money after costs, and the costs are structural (2026-11-23, note `forex-trend-across-the-10-pairs`, the first forex trial; forex pool 1 trial, 875 across all pools).
lessons.text: Textbook 12-month time-series momentum (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012) across the 10 pairs, each sized to 3% volatility, capped at 3x gross, 2006-02 to 2022-12, 500 AUD: -30.2% (CAGR -2.1%), Sharpe -0.07 (95% CI -0.55 to 0.40), max drawdown -58%, underwater for 14 of the 17 years, Sharpe above zero in 2 of 8 two-year windows. It fails every test its note set. Before costs it made about +2.3% a year (Sharpe 0.16, checked by hand against the engine), in line with reports that currency momentum faded after 2008. Costs took more than that: spreads 106 AUD and financing -176 AUD, chiefly the broker's markup, about 1% a year on a book averaging 2.8x gross, so roughly 2.8% of equity a year before any carry. The general lesson for forex at retail CFD terms: a strategy must earn more than its gross exposure times the markup, every year, before it earns anything; leverage multiplies that drag, not just the returns. Turnover was 46x equity a year (daily volatility rescaling through a 2% band per pair).

lessons.title: Forex carry collected its interest and lost far more to the 2008 crash (2026-11-23, note `forex-carry-across-the-10-pairs`; forex pool 2 trials, luck bar 0.11; 876 across all pools).
lessons.text: Hold each pair towards its higher yield where the published rate difference beats the 1% markup, 3% volatility per pair, monthly, 2006-02 to 2022-12, 500 AUD: -50.2% (CAGR -4.0%), Sharpe -0.37 (P(true Sharpe > 0) 6%), max drawdown -60%, skew -1.0 and kurtosis 30, 2 of 8 two-year windows. It fails every test its note set. The mechanism worked: financing earned +103 AUD and spreads cost 5. Prices took ~350: +5% in 2006, -13% in 2007 and -47% in 2008 as carry trades unwound together, then near-zero rates left a small book (0.4-1x gross) drifting a few percent either way to 2022. That is the published crash risk of carry (Brunnermeier, Nagel and Pedersen 2008), taken at its worst point and never earned back at retail terms. Its daily returns correlated -0.11 with the rejected trend run: a different bet, equally unpaid. Two textbook forex premia, run once each at retail CFD costs, both lost from 2006.

lessons.title: After a Coinbase listing, nothing tradable is left (2026-11-23, note `does-a-coinbase-listing-move-a-coin-on-binance`; a raw-effect study, not a trial).
lessons.text: Every Binance coin outside the locked half that Coinbase listed after it had 60 days on Binance, 2019 to 2025-10: 72 events on 58 listing days. Against the other coins, day 1 to day 31: mean -1.7%, P(< 0) 63%, 72% of events below zero, and 34% of placebo means as low: KILL (two-sided, 95% needed either way). The move comes before the listing (day -30 to day 1: +25.6% against the other coins, reported, deciding nothing), as the published studies found (Li, Luo, Wang and Wei 2025; Laucht's cross-listing study): by the time a Binance trader can see the listing, the effect is spent. Most events lag, but a few big winners pull the mean back towards zero; by year it swings from +15% (2020, 6 events) to -27% (2023, 2), too few each to read. Not an exit rule either, unlike a coin's first perp listing (-15%).

lessons.title: The trend rules' timing beats their own weights at random times on ETH and SOL, not quite on BTC (2026-11-26, `kestrel random-timing`; a control, not a trial, information only).
lessons.text: Each paper-traded one-coin strategy against 200 copies of its own weights rotated in time (same exposure, holding lengths, trades and costs; only the alignment with the market lost), on its backtest period before the holdout: | Strategy | Market | Sharpe after costs | Copies' median, 95th pct | Beats | |---|---|---|---|---| | btc-regime-trend | ETH | 1.33 | 0.58, 1.10 | 100% | | btc-regime-trend | SOL | 1.72 | 0.69, 1.35 | 100% | | trend-vol-target | SOL | 1.52 | 0.95, 1.43 | 98% | | trend-vol-target | ETH | 1.24 | 0.75, 1.18 | 97% | | trend-vol-target | BTC | 1.23 | 0.76, 1.28 | 94% | | stablecoin-vol-hold | ETH | 0.87 | 0.45, 0.93 | 90% | | stablecoin-vol-hold | BTC | 0.87 | 0.57, 1.05 | 78% | So the timing itself carries information, most clearly for the BTC regime rule, which is stricter than test 1 (the copies pay the strategy's own costs; holding doesn't). It doesn't undo the luck test: that counts every trial ever run, this asks one question of one strategy. Seven markets tested at 95% each, so one pass in seven could be chance. A rotation also moves the volatility sizing off the days it was measured on, so "timing" here includes sizing. stablecoin-vol-hold's timing can't be told from random, which fits its `watch` decision. btc-rotation-8 (a basket) isn't covered.

lessons.title: The BTC regime rule's two trend filters stand in for each other: either one is enough, neither alone earns its place (2026-11-26, note `which-part-of-the-btc-regime-rule-carries-it`; 8 trials, information only, no decision changes).
lessons.text: btc-regime-trend with each part switched off in turn (`btc-regime-ablation`; all on is the rule exactly), on its own periods (ETH 2020-01, SOL 2020-08, to 2025-10), after costs: | Variant | ETH Sharpe | Max DD | Exposure | Trades | Beats random timing | SOL Sharpe | Max DD | Exposure | Trades | Beats random timing | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Full rule (existing runs) | 1.33 | -35% | 34% | 360 | 100% | 1.72 | -32% | 23% | 307 | 100% | | (a) no BTC filter | 1.34 | -33% | 39% | 423 | 100% | 1.68 | -33% | 27% | 362 | 99% | | (b) no coin trend | 1.44 | -38% | 41% | 388 | 99% | 1.64 | -46% | 30% | 399 | 100% | | (c) fully in, no vol sizing | 1.39 | -47% | 45% | 140 | 100% | 1.80 | -48% | 42% | 104 | 100% | | (d) neither filter (vol-hold) | 1.06 | -65% | 69% | 526 | 85% | 1.19 | -76% | 52% | 576 | 43% | | Holding (test 1) | 1.12 | | | | | 1.24 | | | | | By the note's rule (a part earns its place when removing it lowers the Sharpe by more than 0.1), no single part does, on either coin: every one-part change moves the Sharpe by 0.11 or less, and taking out the coin's trend *raises* it on ETH. Taking out both filters costs 0.27 (ETH) and 0.53 (SOL) and leaves the timing no better than random. So the rule's edge is being out of the market while trends are down, and either trend measure does that; what the pair adds over one is shallower drawdowns (SOL's -46% with the BTC filter alone, -32% with both). The hypothesis (the BTC filter carries most of it) is not supported; by its own falsification test (on both coins, removing the coin trend costs more than removing the BTC filter) it is not falsified either: true on SOL, not on ETH. The volatility sizing came out as expected: Sharpe within 0.1 either way, drawdown about 13 to 16 points deeper fully in. vol-hold stays near holding, as on BTC (findings 2). Differences this size are well inside a five-year Sharpe's sampling error, and all of it is pre-holdout data that was searched (SOL and ETH) and already deflated-Sharpe-failing; the paper accounts keep the full rule. A simpler one-filter version would be a new note on fresh data, never a swap made from this table.

lessons.title: An independent rebuild of the BTC regime rule matches ours except in each coin's first 19 days (2026-11-26; a check of the code, not a trial).
lessons.text: A fresh agent got only the confirmation note's rule wording and daily bars for three exploration-half coins (1INCH, AAVE, AION, the last delisted in 2023) and BTC. It never saw our code or any result, and wrote its own version in plain Python. Its target weights against ours, bar by bar: AION matches on all 1,105 bars (largest difference 2e-15). 1INCH and AAVE match on every bar but 19 each, all at the start: the rebuild holds from a coin's 31st bar, ours from its 50th. The cause is ours: BTC's 50-day average is computed over the BTC closes attached to the coin's own bars, so it waits for 50 days of the *coin's* history, while the wording ("btc_close is above its 50-day average"; BTC has years of history) allows the 31st. Ours is the stricter of the two (more days in cash, never a lookahead), and AION matched only because its coin trend was off on those days anyway. What it touches: each coin's first 19 days in the confirmation run and in the backtests that start at a coin's listing (SOL from 2020-08), and the first 19 days of backtests whose data starts at their start date (ETH 2020-01). Not the paper accounts, which read years of history. The rebuild listed 23 places the wording left a choice; on every other one exercised here (a simple average including today, strict comparisons, the close exactly 30 days earlier, sample volatility of 30 log returns times sqrt(365), cash on zero volatility) the two agree. One choice not exercised: across a gap in a coin's history the rebuild holds cash, while ours counts bars, not days; none of the three coins has a gap. The code is the frozen implementation and stays as it is; the wording and the code now differ in a recorded way.

lessons.title: One-coin backtests compute straight across a gap in a coin's history, and say nothing (2026-11-26; an independent rebuild of trend-vol-target; a check of the code, not a trial).
lessons.text: A second fresh agent rebuilt trend-vol-target from its first note's wording on three exploration-half coins, one clean (ATOM) and two with gaps it wasn't told about: STRAX (8 days missing in 2024-03, after which the price is exactly a tenth of the last close, at 160 times the volume: a token swap) and CVC (154 days, delisted 2022-12 and relisted 2023-05). It found both, split each coin at its gaps and computed nothing across one. Against ours: ATOM matches on all 2,378 bars (largest difference 3e-16); STRAX differs on 22 bars and CVC on 51, all in the 120 days after the gap, all ours holding (on average 20% and 40%) where the rebuild was in cash. Ours counts bars, so after a gap its votes compare prices from the two sides of it. The panel used by universe and basket strategies already numbers unbroken histories and computes nothing across a gap (docs/rules.md); one-coin backtests, and `kestrel confirm`, read the raw bars and neither refuse nor report one. BTC, ETH and SOL daily bars have no gap, so no pursued result or paper account is touched (at any bar size). The confirmation run (Luke's OK to read gap dates and the price across each gap, never returns): 6 of its 180 coins had one. Four are token swaps or a reused symbol, not missing days: BNX (the price a hundredth after 5 days), COCOS (a thousand times, 3 days), VIDT (about a tenth, 8 days) and LUNA (20,000 times: the original coin, then LUNA 2.0). FTT (310 days) and KEY (27) were relistings. Their numbers were computed across the gap, so they are void, but neither verdict can move: btc-regime-trend's PASS needed more than half on both tests, and with all 6 coins' wins counted as losses it is still 144 of 180 coins (80%) and 416 of 771 windows (54%); crash-rebound's FAIL (274 of 771 windows) can't reach half even if all 27 of their windows won. Fixed the same day (Luke): the one-coin engines refuse bars with a day or more missing and name the histories; `kestrel confirm` runs a coin with a gap on its latest unbroken history (the coin as it trades now) and lists it; an outage of hours (BTC and ETH lost two 4h bars on 2020-02-19) isn't a gap. Saved runs aren't rerun.

lessons.title: Falls with forced perp selling bounce more than other falls, but not by enough to tell at 95%: KILL (2026-11-26, note do-falls-with-forced-perp-selling-bounce-more v2, `kestrel event-study oi-flush`; a study, not a trial).
lessons.text: From the deep research's top lead. 63 coins with Binance perps (open interest in contracts, from 2021-12-01, outside the locked half), to 2025-10. A flush is a spot fall on a day open interest dropped sharply (z below -2 against the coin's previous 90 days); each is compared with falls of the same size without one, both bought at the next open and held 5 days, after costs: | Test (all needed) | Result | | |---|---|---| | 1. Excess over matched falls, 95% interval by date | +1.60% a flush, [-0.12%, +3.31%] | **Fail** | | 2. Beats the same coins on random days | +1.28% net against a 95th percentile of +0.26% | Pass | | 3. At least 30 distinct dates | 1,023 flushes on 452 dates | Pass | By the note's rule this is KILL, and the note says what that means: flush falls can't be told from ordinary falls at 95%, so on this evidence it is dip-buying under another name and dies with that family. The point estimate is positive and the interval only just reaches below zero; that is recorded, not used. Deciding nothing: BTC, ETH and SOL apart +1.69% (87 flushes); by year +0.86% (2022), +0.10% (2023), +3.27% (2024), +1.59% (2025); flushes on days BTC fell too +2.00% (811) against +0.09% for a coin alone (212), a pattern nobody predicted, so a lead for a new note at most, never a finding; trend-vol-target on the same coin was in cash on 33% of flush days. 4,237 coin-days (about 5%) had no open-interest close and were skipped. The run was repeated once after fixing an information-only counter (it had counted days before the archive began as missing: 48,494); the seeded tests and verdict were identical. The archive starts in 2021-12, so more history can only come from time going forward. Note rejected (Luke, 2026-11-26).

lessons.title: Backtests now warm up on history before their start, and G1 beats its own coins held equally (2026-11-26; the strategy review's items b and c).
lessons.text: A backtest used to load no bars before its start, so a rule sat in cash while its lookback filled and holding was invested from day one (trend-vol-target on BTC 121 days; G1 427, while BTC fell 72%). Now the strategy reads up to 400 days before the start, read only: the account opens with its cash at the start and trades from the next open, as holding does. A coin listed later is scored, with holding, from when the lookback has filled (SOL from 2020-12-09 for trend-vol-target, 2020-09-30 for the regime rule; G1 from 2018-08-17). A robustness grid scores every setting and holding over the same days. Re-scored, Sharpe (holding) old → new: trend-vol-target BTC 1.23 (1.07) → 1.24 (1.07), ETH 1.24 (1.12) → 1.29 (1.12), SOL 1.52 (1.24) → 1.58 (1.41); btc-regime-trend ETH 1.33 (1.12) → 1.48 (1.12), SOL 1.72 (1.24) → 1.75 (1.28); G1 1.55 (BTC 0.74) → 1.57 (0.94); trend-trio 1.59 → 1.61 (1.07); stablecoin-vol-hold 0.87 → 0.85 on BTC (0.74) and ETH (0.68). Deflated 0-9% throughout. No scorecard verdict moves on any of the nine. Robustness, rerun for the five with open notes, stays ROBUST (19/19, 19/19, 15/16, 15/16 and 22/22 neighbours beat holding over the grid's days). The five runs were saved again; the other three have rejected notes and were re-scored unsaved. Two reruns were first saved under the regime note's v2 (which says v1's runs stand), counting as two new trials; they were deleted within a minute. The count is unchanged by the reruns; the bar moved 2.28 → 2.29 as warmed Sharpes replaced old ones. G1 against its own coins (fixed in the to-do list before the run: each of its 8 coins 1/8 of equity once a year old, rebalanced each Sunday, no signal; `own-8-basket`, one trial): over the same 2,633 days, Sharpe 1.57 against 1.08 after costs, a pass of test 1 against the control docs/rules.md asks of a universe strategy. At G1's 29% exposure the basket made +298% against +3,608%; its drawdown -79% against -37%; daily correlation 0.64. Both share the coin list's survivorship (findings 15), so this says the regime and ranking add to holding these coins, not that they were knowable in 2018. G1 deflates to 2% at 881 trials (bar 2.29). Its frozen own-coins note (btc-regime-rotation-g1-on-its-own-coins) names BTC held as the benchmark, against docs/rules.md; the note stays as written, and its test 1 is now read against both. Follow-ups the same day: the decay check's reference backtest is warmed too; a new research strategy must declare its warm-up (37 older ones are listed as exempt, a list that only shrinks); and a backtest refuses an unchanged setup already saved under an older version of its note unless told it is a new trial (`--as-new-trial`).

lessons.title: G1's rule still beats BTC and its own basket on coins picked at the time, but the hindsight list carried about half its margin (2026-11-26, note does-g1-s-rule-work-on-coins-picked-at-the-time, 2 trials).
lessons.text: G1's rule unchanged, but each Sunday it may hold only that week's 8 coins with the highest 30-day median volume and a year of history (45 different coins over the period), from every coin the engine may use, delisted ones included. Over the same 2,633 days from 2018-08-17, after costs: | Test (both needed) | Result | | |---|---|---| | A. Sharpe beats BTC held | 1.08 vs 0.94 (+702% vs +162% for BTC at its 25% exposure) | Pass | | B. Sharpe beats the same weekly top 8 held equally | 1.08 vs 0.65 (basket drawdown -86%) | Pass | By the note's rule the list did not make G1's backtest: the rule works on coins it could have picked then. Deciding nothing: G1 on its own coins scores 1.57 over the same days, so the hindsight list carried about half of its margin over BTC (0.63 of Sharpe against 0.14 here); worst drawdown -38%; in the market 169 of 376 weeks, mostly BTC, ETH and BNB (60, 58 and 58 weeks), SOL 46, LTC 38; daily correlation 0.84 with G1's own-coins run. Deflated 0.1% at 883 trials (bar 2.29): it passes neither luck nor anything out of sample, and G1's settings were searched on this data. The locked confirmation half (XRP, ADA, AVAX and others) was out of the candidates, as for every universe run.

lessons.title: Every saved run re-scored with warm-up: six test 1 results flip to pass, no note's verdict moves (2026-11-26; a re-measurement, not trials).
lessons.text: All 166 saved strategy runs were re-run with the history before their start (findings 33), unsaved; the record keeps the originals, and the figures are kept outside the repository. None failed to reproduce. Median Sharpe change +0.03 (holding's 0.00); the biggest moves are short or late-starting runs, where the cold start was a large share of the period: trend-vol-target's one-year 2024-10 runs (BTC -0.35 → 1.12), the 52-week-high basket (0.11 → 0.78), BTC and gold (0.54 → 1.00), and the 5-minute methods (still deeply negative). Test 1 flips from fail to pass on six runs, never the other way: trend-vol-target on SOL 1h (1.47 vs 1.41) and SOL 4h over the year from 2024-10 (0.70 vs 0.63), the 4h-volatile-regime note's runs on BTC, ETH and SOL (plain trend-vol-target over its later period), and the ablation's no-BTC-filter variant on ETH (1.21 vs 1.12). None changes a note's own test: the regime filter still loses to plain trend-vol-target on every coin (BTC 0.69 vs 1.04, ETH 0.72 vs 0.99, SOL 0.66 vs 1.23), and every ablation variant moved by about the same amount (ETH about +0.15, SOL about +0.02), so the order behind findings 29 is unchanged. The near misses stay misses (52-week high 0.78 vs holding 1.07; BTC and gold 1.00 vs 1.01). With the warmed Sharpes in place of the saved ones the luck bar is unchanged (2.29 at 883 trials: runs are a small share of the trials, most of which are grid settings). The robustness grids saved before 2026-11-26 were not re-scored.
